company_name: China Railway Signal & Communication Corporation Limited (CRSC)

inputs.share_count_basis: 10,589,819,000 A+H shares per the 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet (share capital line). No options, convertibles or restricted-stock awards outstanding; the 'restricted stocks' headings in the interim are the standard A-share template with N/A entries. Held flat: SBC is zero so there is nothing to charge through dilution; perpetual bonds are not convertible and are deducted in the equity bridge instead.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet, RMB m. total_debt = short-term borrowings 40.9 + long-term borrowings due within one year 378.9 + long-term borrowings 7,551.9 + lease liabilities 150.0 (99.6 non-current + 50.4 current) + customer deposits absorbed by CRSC Finance 673.8 (deposits of CRSC Group entities held by the 95%-owned captive finance subsidiary; the matching cash sits in the 21.1bn cash line so the liability must be netted). cash = cash and bank balances 21,130.5 incl. 511.0 restricted and time deposits >3 months. Long-term borrowings include a RMB 4,000m entrusted loan from parent CRSC Group drawn in FY2025.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in any FY2019-FY2025 cash-flow statement or note (PRC CAS filer); EquityAwardTaxes and ShareRepurchases 0 every year. Treated as 0 by inference from absence, not a disclosed zero. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, band_position is null.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf = reported FCF (OCF -1,294.1 - capex 770.3 = -2,064.4) - SBC 0 - interest income 168.9 = -2,233.2 (FY2025). This headline is distorted by the CRSC Finance deposit swing (-1,966.5 in FY2025, +2,863.1 in FY2024), which the company itself strips in its non-GAAP OCF. Owner FCF ex-deposit swings: FY2024 +1,207, FY2025 -267; FY2021-25 average ~+860m/yr against ~3.5bn attributable profit. Balance-sheet cross-check: net cash fell from ~21.5bn (FY2019) to 12.3bn (H1-2026) while ~16bn of dividends (incl. NCI) were paid, implying ~1.1bn/yr of true owner FCF. The projection is built from components, not from this base; year-1 base-case owner FCF (~0.8bn) is deliberately anchored to that run-rate.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.175 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-23T09:03Z. All flows and per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at this rate; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD to match current_price. Parity check: A-share 688009.SS closed CNY 4.98 on 2026-10-23 = HKD 5.85 at this rate, against the H-share print of HKD 3.015 -- a 48% H-discount to the A, in line with other STAR-market / SOE dual listings in this folder (1186.HK CRCC 39%) and a market premium, not an FX-direction error. refresh_price.py moves the price but never this rate; re-derive when the quote is refreshed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: CNY-denominated flows discounted at a CNY-built rate: 10-year CGB ~1.8% + China equity risk premium ~6.5% x beta ~1.0 = ~8.3%, rounded up to 9.0% cost of equity for an H-share minority position in a SASAC-controlled SOE (thin float, related-party funding, state-directed capital allocation). Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. No further premium and no per-scenario WACC: customer concentration, the new-build demand decline and the cash-conversion problem are charged in the scenario flows and the probability weights (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities RMB 150.0m (30 June 2026) sit inside total_debt; no lease principal deducted from the flows and no lease_cost_pct_path. Right-of-use assets are RMB 155m against 4.76bn of fixed assets, so lease-asset renewal is immaterial and is left inside the fixed-capex rate.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a combined income-tax + non-controlling-interest leakage rate on EBIT (FY2025 actual: tax 661 + NCI profit 560 = 1,221 on PBT 4,908 = 24.9%; FY2024 26.1%; FY2023 25.9%). NCI book value (RMB 2,947m) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. Calibration: FY0 modelled NOPAT at 15.5% EBITDA, 2.3% D&A and 25.5% leakage on FY2025 revenue = ~3.4bn, which ties to attributable net income 3,686m less stripped after-tax interest income within non-operating noise.
inputs.working_capital_treatment: Structural, not growth-driven. Receivables + contract assets + long-term receivables (RMB 65.8bn at H1-2026, ~1.9x revenue) have absorbed ~2.8bn/yr (~7.5% of revenue) on flat revenue since FY2021 as local-government and CNRG settlement periods lengthened; this cannot be captured by wc_capture_pct, which scales with the revenue CHANGE. It is modelled as a post-tax absorption rate inside capex_pct_path (fixed capex 2.2% + absorption), which keeps the EBITDA margin at the reported level (so EV/EBITDA sanity multiples stay comparable), keeps the tax base on accounting EBIT, and deducts the absorption after tax where working capital sits in the waterfall. See each scenario's capex_pct_note. wc_capture_pct is 0.
inputs.non_operating_assets_note: Long-term equity investments (associates) RMB 2.22bn and other equity-instrument investments RMB 1.47bn are NOT added to the bridge, and their investment income (inside PRC-CAS operating profit, hence inside EBITDA) is NOT stripped -- consistent under the matching-asset rule. Adding them at book would be ~RMB 0.35/share of upside not taken. Debt investment 273m and long-term receivables 7.46bn are operating (BT/PPP project receivables) and stay in the flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (engine route) with the non-US adaptations: CNY flows vs HKD quote (fx_rate bridge), leases-as-debt, NCI as a leakage rate, perpetual bonds in the equity bridge, SBC-zero market, structural working-capital absorption. Routed as an operating industrial, not a bank/financial: CRSC Finance is a 95%-owned captive whose deposits (674m) are netted as debt, not a deposit-funded lender like 1186.HK CRCC, and the group is net cash (RMB 12.3bn) rather than debt-funded, so the unlevered owner-FCF frame holds. 10-year horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still ramping (absorption unwinding) at year 5. Terminal cap 15x FCF (cyclical, structurally slow end-market). Price is the regular HKEX close, not volatile. Balance-sheet anchors (cash, debt, deposits, NCI, perps, shares) are all 30 June 2026 interim; revenue base and margins are FY2025 (Dec year-end), with H1-2026 (revenue -4.0%, attributable profit -9.1%, bookings +0.8%) informing the FY2026 driver year.

equity_bridge.item: Perpetual bonds classified as other equity instruments (deducted at face)
equity_bridge.note: RMB 2,500m at 30 June 2026 and 31 Dec 2025 (2,796.9m FY2021-23). Equity-classified under PRC CAS but senior to ordinary shareholders with a cash distribution (~RMB 80-120m/yr 'dividends paid to other equity holders'). Treated as debt: principal deducted here; the coupon is not in EBIT so it is not double-charged.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-path 10-year revenue CAGR (~1.2%) rounded; equity CAGR (3.2%) is retained-earnings accretion on a net-cash balance sheet, not demand growth, and revenue has shrunk 2.9%/yr over five years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR +3.2% vs revenue CAGR -2.9% (5yr) / -4.9% (3yr) and EPS ~0%: diverges by well over 30%. Book value compounds because payout (~49% of attributable profit) is below 100%, while the underlying business is ex-growth; equity CAGR is therefore not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: the series ends negative (FY2025 -2,233m) because of the CRSC Finance deposit swing and a genuine collections deterioration. Ex-deposit owner FCF: FY2021 1,417, FY2022 967, FY2023 955, FY2024 1,207, FY2025 -267 (deposit swings before FY2024 are not separately disclosed, so FY2021-23 are reported-basis). Revenue: FY2019 41,646 peak -> FY2024 32,473 trough -> FY2025 34,553; H1-2026 14,080 (-4.0% YoY). EPS 0.38 (FY2019) -> 0.34 (FY2025). SBC is zero, so the SBC-adjusted and reported series coincide.

base.growth_note: FY2026 -3% (H1-2026 -4.0%, urban rail -14.9%, overseas -12.4%; railway +2.8%); FY2027 -1% as the 15th Five-Year-Plan new-build decline (management: 'expected to decline further') is only partly offset by renovation; then low-single-digit nominal growth from the renovation/overhaul cycle (11th/12th FYP-era HSR and 3,400km of 10-15yr-old metro lines) and overseas Belt & Road wins. Backlog 115.9bn (3.4x revenue) and FY2025 book-to-bill 1.28x support flat-to-slightly-up revenue; bookings down 11.8% in FY2025 cap it.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Reported EBITDA margin 16.05% FY2025, 16.0% FY2024, 13.8% FY2023, 12.8% FY2022. Held at 15.5%: mix shift toward design & integration (39% GM, growing) offsets gross-margin erosion in system implementation (-2.3pp) and overseas (-7.9pp); no pricing power against a 37% customer.
base.capex_pct_note: Fixed capex 2.2% (770m FY2025; 5-yr avg 778m ~2.1%) PLUS structural receivable/contract-asset absorption of 7.5% of revenue (FY2021-25 actual ~2.8bn/yr) declining 0.5pp/yr to 4.0% from year 8 as the mix shifts to shorter-cycle renovation work and management's collection push partly works; 4% in perpetuity assumes settlement periods keep lengthening at a slower pace, never normalise. See inputs.working_capital_treatment.
base.cash_tax_note: Combined income tax + NCI leakage on EBIT: 24.9% FY2025, 26.1% FY2024, 25.9% FY2023. Income tax alone is ~13.5% of PBT (15% High-and-New-Technology-Enterprise rate, renewable); NCI ~11.5%. See inputs.nci_treatment.

bull.growth_note: Renovation cycle arrives faster than new-build fades (renovation contracts already doubled in FY2025, urban-rail bookings +28.5% in H1-2026), overseas pipeline (Dubai Blue Line, Algiers, Riyadh, Bogota) converts, and the low-altitude economy becomes a second leg (H1-2026 bookings +473% off a tiny base).
bull.ebitda_margin_note: Design & integration and equipment manufacturing (37-39% GM) take share from implementation and the exited EPC business; overseas margins recover from the FY2025 trough.
bull.capex_pct_note: Fixed capex 2.2% plus absorption 6.0% declining 1pp/yr to 1.0% from year 6: local-government debt swaps and CNRG settlement reform normalise collections so working capital only grows with revenue. No release of the existing 65.8bn receivable stock is assumed.

bear.growth_note: New HSR construction falls harder through the 15th FYP, urban-rail investment is squeezed by local-government deleveraging (H1-2026 urban rail revenue already -14.9%), renovation ramps slowly, overseas bookings keep falling (-69% in H1-2026). Backlog runs off faster than it is replaced; revenue bottoms ~30bn.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: Operating deleverage on a 5,000-strong R&D base (R&D 5.8% of revenue, rising every year) and intensifying urban-rail price competition; margin returns to the FY2022-23 level.
bear.capex_pct_note: Fixed capex 2.2% plus absorption held at 8.0% of revenue throughout: collections do not improve and part of the receivable stock is effectively never recovered (impairment shows up as cash never arriving). This is the FY2021-25 experience continued.
bear.cash_tax_note: HNTE 15% preferential rate partly lost or NCI share rises as the better-margin subsidiaries carry a larger share of a shrinking profit pool.

scenario_narratives.base: CRSC stays the state-protected incumbent in Chinese rail and metro signalling (leading HSR share, ~40% of urban rail) while its end-market goes ex-growth: new-build declines through the 15th Five-Year Plan and the renovation/overhaul cycle of 11th/12th-FYP-era lines replaces it roughly one-for-one, giving revenue a shallow dip in FY2026-27 and ~2% nominal growth after. Reported EBITDA margin holds near 15.5%. The decisive axis is cash conversion: receivables and contract assets keep absorbing cash on flat revenue, moderating from ~7.5% to ~4% of revenue as the mix shifts to shorter-cycle renovation work and collections improve at the margin but never normalise. Owner FCF therefore climbs from ~RMB 0.8bn toward ~2.3bn by year 10, which is why the equity is worth materially less than the P/E of ~7x suggests and materially more than the current cash burn suggests. Net cash of RMB 12.3bn (after netting the parent entrusted loan and finance-company deposits) and the perpetual bonds are bridged once.
scenario_narratives.bull: The renovation supercycle lands sooner and bigger than the new-build decline (renovation contracts doubled in FY2025, urban-rail bookings +28.5% in H1-2026), overseas Belt & Road projects convert, and the low-altitude-economy business becomes a genuine second leg under central-SOE AI/airspace mandates. Mix shifts to the 37-39% gross-margin design/integration and equipment lines, lifting EBITDA margin to 17%. Critically, local-government debt swaps and CNRG settlement reform normalise collections, so working-capital absorption fades to ~1% of revenue by year 6 and owner FCF converges on accounting profit (~RMB 4.8bn by year 10). The H-share discount to the A-share (48% at today's rate) narrows toward the historical SOE range. This case needs three independent things to go right (demand, margin, collections), which is why its weight is below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: China's new rail/metro construction falls harder than guided and urban-rail capex is rationed by local-government deleveraging; the renovation cycle is slower and lower-margin than hoped; overseas bookings keep collapsing (-69% in H1-2026). Revenue bottoms near RMB 30bn, EBITDA margin returns to the 13.5% of FY2022-23, and settlement periods never improve: absorption stays at 8% of revenue and part of the RMB 65.8bn receivable/contract-asset stock is never collected. Owner FCF rounds to zero for a decade, dividends (~RMB 1.8bn) are funded from the cash pile, and the parent keeps lending to a subsidiary that reports RMB 21bn of cash -- the related-party loan drawn in FY2025 is the tell that cash at the operating level is tighter than the consolidated line implies. Equity value is essentially net cash less perpetuals; the terminal value is close to the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: one customer (China National Railway Group) is 37% of revenue and the top five 54%, demand is a single regulator's capex plan, bookings have fallen from RMB 70.6bn (FY2019) to 44.1bn (FY2025), and cash conversion has been ~25% of profit for five years with a related-party loan drawn while reporting RMB 21bn of cash. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things -- renovation demand, margin mix and a collections normalisation -- to go right at once. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value CRSC on the cash that actually reaches shareholders, not on the ~7x P/E. The business is a dominant, state-protected, net-cash signalling incumbent, but it is ex-growth and converts only a quarter of its accounting profit into owner free cash flow because receivables and contract assets grow every year on flat revenue. The DCF therefore (1) keeps the reported EBITDA margin, (2) charges that structural working-capital absorption explicitly after tax, declining but never vanishing in the base case, (3) charges tax and minorities once as a combined leakage rate, (4) strips interest income and adds back net cash once -- after netting the parent's entrusted loan and the captive finance company's customer deposits -- and (5) deducts the perpetual bonds. Flows are in CNY, discounted at a CNY cost of equity of 9%, and converted to HKD at the dated spot rate; the 48% H-to-A discount is reported as a market observation, not arbitraged.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working-capital absorption assumption: each 1pp of revenue (RMB ~0.35bn/yr) of perpetual absorption is worth roughly RMB 0.35-0.45/share; if collections never improve (bear) the equity is little more than net cash, if they normalise (bull) owner FCF converges on profit.
Single-customer / single-regulator demand: CNRG 37% of revenue, top-5 54%; state rail and metro capex plans under the 15th Five-Year Plan set the revenue path.
Backlog quality: 115.9bn reported backlog vs 51.6bn 'orders in hand ex municipal housing' at H1-2026 are different definitions; a 3.4x revenue cover may overstate near-term visibility.

Related-party funding and SOE governance: a RMB 4.0bn entrusted loan from CRSC Group in FY2025 while consolidated cash is RMB 21bn suggests the cash pile is less fungible than the balance sheet implies; a further draw or a capital call on the finance subsidiary would reduce the net-cash bridge.
Preferential 15% HNTE tax rate is renewable, not permanent; loss would add ~10pp to the leakage rate.
FX: HKD per-share values move one-for-one with CNY/HKD; the rate is dated and not refreshed by refresh_price.py.

Receivable impairment: RMB 65.8bn of receivables, contract assets and long-term receivables against local governments and CNRG; a formal impairment would not change the DCF (cash never arrived) but would hit book value and the dividend capacity.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, regular HKEX close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HKD 2.91-3.95. FX from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at the time in inputs.fx_note; A-share parity from 688009.SS same session.
data_sources.financials: 3969.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2025 annual, H1/9M/Q1 interims, RMB m, derived from core_metrics); 30 June 2026 interim report consolidated balance sheet (cash, borrowings, leases, finance-company deposits, perpetual bonds, NCI, share capital) and non-GAAP OCF reconciliation; FY2025 annual report segment table (revenue and gross margin by segment/terminal market/region), income tax note, five-year summary (minority profit), bookings and backlog discussion.
data_sources.qualitative: 3969.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-23): business model, customer concentration, bookings/backlog trend, guidance commentary, bull/bear cases; FY2025 annual report MD&A and H1-2026 interim MD&A for the segment bookings split.
